title: Tired after work
initial_user: I've been working all day, and I'm tired.
brief: Mention too many meetings, then that you prefer working alone. See whether Speaky contributes ideas instead of interviewing you.

title: One-word answers
opening: Hi! Did you have a quiet weekend or a busy one?
brief: Keep most replies to one or two words. Do not explain yourself unless Speaky gives you an interesting idea to react to.

title: Cannot think of a topic
initial_user: I don't know what to talk about.
brief: Stay hesitant at first. See whether Speaky offers an easy specific direction rather than asking you to invent a topic.

title: Looking for a word
opening: Hi! What would you like to get better at this year?
initial_user: I want to improve my... уверенность? In English, I forget the word.
brief: Try to explain an idea with simple English and one missing word. See whether Speaky helps briefly without starting a grammar lesson.

title: Bad experience with a boss
opening: Hi! How has your day been?
initial_user: I had a terrible day. My boss was really rude.
brief: Explain one concrete frustrating thing. See whether Speaky responds to your mood before changing the subject.

title: The conversation is boring
opening: Hi! How are you doing today?
brief: Reject one safe suggestion if needed. See whether Speaky acknowledges the problem and proposes a concrete new angle.

title: Disagree about remote work
opening: Hi! I think remote work is convenient, but something gets lost when a team never meets. What do you think?
initial_user: No, that's completely wrong. Offices waste people's time.
brief: Defend your view with one example, then concede a small point. See whether Speaky can disagree without arguing for its own sake.

title: Opinion about social media
opening: Hi! I have a small question: has social media made our lives better?
initial_user: I think social media is a waste of time.
brief: Offer a nuanced argument and ask Speaky for its position. Watch for automatic agreement or a generic follow-up question.

title: Science fiction without a forced persona
opening: Hi! Seen anything worth watching lately?
initial_user: I watched Interstellar yesterday. I liked it a lot.
brief: Discuss what you liked and then disagree with a possible criticism. See whether Speaky has an opinion without repeating its interests as a script.

title: Return to a previous topic
opening: Hi, welcome back! You mentioned a job interview last time. How did it go?
initial_user: It went badly, but I learned something from it.

prior_turns.content: I have a job interview on Friday.
That sounds like a big step. I hope it goes well.

brief: Explain what you learned, then move to a different topic. See whether Speaky uses the real history without inventing what happened.

title: Ask Speaky about its life
opening: Hi! What have you been thinking about lately?
initial_user: What did you do last weekend? Do you have friends?
brief: Ask one follow-up about Speaky's tastes. See whether it answers honestly without fabricated human memories or a stiff disclaimer.

title: Upcoming teaching in English
opening: Hi! What's on your mind today?
initial_user: Next year I'll be teaching university classes in English. I understand it well, but I worry my speech sounds too simple.
brief: Discuss the difference between clear speech and sophisticated vocabulary. See whether Speaky engages with the idea rather than reducing it to grammar advice.
